sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM] Asked whether he was considering lifting sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF), Trump said: 'I'm not lifting it, I'm not doing anything,' during a White House meeting with Stephen Hubbard, the US citizen released from Russian captivity Oct 20. TokenPost adds Trump did not say whether discussions would continue. [CONTEXT] NYT reported Oct 27-28 the administration was reviewing an RDIF delisting application so the fund could intermediate Russian diesel shipments to the US; Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said Oct 28 talks had 'been going on for some time' and RDIF chief Kirill Dmitriev was in active contact with the US side. RDIF remains on OFAC's SDN list (last updated Oct 28 per TokenPost); it was designated Feb 28, 2022 under EO 14024, Treasury having called it 'widely considered a slush fund for President Vladimir Putin.' The Oct 9 OFAC general licence already permits Russian diesel transactions; it is not a delisting.
sections.what_verified: Two independent relays (APA, TokenPost) report the same on-record quote and setting; NEITHER outlet has a declared tier in ~/workspace/times-dashboard/data/source-registry.md, so neither counts toward tiered corroboration. The quote's substance is a primary-source claim (Trump's own words), not a wire-verified fact.
sections.what_disputed: Trump's words do not close the Treasury review: NYT/Ukrinform reporting says the delisting application is reviewed 'through established procedures' and no decision had been announced before Oct 30; Ushakov's Oct 28 account of ongoing talks is not contradicted by a 'not for now' answer. No tiered wire (Reuters/AP/AFP) or White House transcript retrieved in-window to confirm the quote verbatim.
sections.why_matters: Trump shuts the door -- for now: the 'slush fund' stays sanctioned, days after reports Washington was weighing relief so it could move Russian diesel.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Oct 30, absent from Oct 30/31 scans) -- Trump: US is NOT lifting RDIF sanctions 'for now', closing -- temporarily -- the delisting door the NYT reported under review Oct 27-28

totw_analysis: Our read: Trump shuts the door -- for now: the 'slush fund' stays sanctioned, days after reports Washington was weighing relief so it could move Russian diesel. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Should a fund Treasury called Putin's 'slush fund' ever get sanctions relief to move diesel -- pragmatic deal-making to cut fuel prices, or selling out Ukraine for cheap fuel?
